references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 13:1–8 · Gifts and sacrifice tested by charity
references.note: In the King James Version, Paul measures eloquence, knowledge, faith, generosity, and sacrifice against charity, then describes its patience, kindness, and freedom from self-seeking. Compare this account with the compilation’s contrast between coercion and love, and with its concrete appeals to gentleness and service. The comparison invites attention to the qualities and effects of love as well as its intensity.

subjects.displayTitle: Future discovery: knowledge and the capacity to use it well
subjects.introduction: A schoolchild today can work out truths that Aristotle never reached, and a child of the telegraph age handles the instrument more easily than its inventor did; yet, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá insists, the merit still belongs to the founders who opened the way. That double movement, confidence in the growth of knowledge joined to gratitude for those who came before, sets the temper for thinking about where discovery is heading. Bahá’u’lláh promises sciences and crafts that no heart has yet conceived, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá speaks of flight, of instant communication, of machines that could give leisure to every worker. He also watched the inventions of his own day turned into engines of slaughter, and prayed that one still-hidden force not be found until spiritual civilization had caught up with material power. Bacon’s imagined research house, whose members deliberate over which findings to publish and pray that their work be put to good use, raises the same question of who judges benefit [1]. The path leads on toward the coming of age of the human race, the ceaseless ascent of material civilization, the mind’s own power of discovery, and religion as the spring from which knowledge flows.
subjects.arc: Begin with cumulative learning, explore the promise and danger of discovery, and end with the patient work of developing capacities and beneficial applications.

order.why: Establish the revisability of scientific understanding.
shortened: For instance, great discoveries and announcements of former centuries are continually upset and discarded by the wise men of today. Mathematicians, astronomers, chemical scientists continually disprove and reject the conclusions of the ancients; nothing is fixed, nothing final; everything is continually changing because human reason is progressing along new roads of investigation and arriving at new conclusions every day. In the future much that is announced and accepted as true now will be rejected and disproved. And so it will continue ad infinitum.

order.why: Open with later knowledge and gratitude to earlier founders.
shortened: In mathematics, school children can now exceed Aristotle in their comprehension of truths. Consider how great is this century, and how magnificent is this era.

Those [earlier] individuals, however, were the founders of sciences and crafts, and as such they should be regarded as superior and be given preference. For example, a child in the telecommunication era is more skilled in handling a telegraph than the inventor himself was; as the inventor could not have transmitted messages with the same ease. The merit nevertheless goes to the preceding and early founders.

order.why: Connect dangerous new power with the need for maturity.
Confront invention used for destruction.
Consider the reported warning about aerial warfare.
Keep the historical discussion of war’s costs in its setting.
Join moral development with material progress.
shortened: If the moral precepts and foundations of divine civilization become united with the material advancement of man, there is no doubt that the happiness of the human world will be attained and that from every direction the glad tidings of peace upon earth will be announced.
Then will the power of the divine make itself effective and the breath of the Holy Spirit penetrate the essence of all things.

order.why: Frame arts and sciences in relation to prosperity.
Open the horizon of sciences not yet imagined.
Read discovery through the language of divine names.
shortened: When the sun of His name, the Creator, dawneth from the horizon of His mouth, through it are made manifest the arts throughout all ages - this is an indubitable truth. This name riseth upon all things that exist, and through it are revealed the arts through the agencies of the kingdom, were ye of them that are assured. All the wondrous and novel manifestations of craftsmanship that ye behold have appeared from this Name, and there shall appear hereafter that which ye have never heard before.

order.why: Consider hidden possibilities within ordinary matter.
Retain the passage about a hidden force without identifying it with a later technology.
Read the reported quotation of the Words of Paradise alongside it.
Keep the reported force within stone in its own terms.
shortened: The edifice of the Most Exalted Shrine shall be expanded. In the future, a form of electricity shall be discovered whereby, within the stone itself and without connection to any power plant, electric lights shall be illuminated.

order.why: Leave the extent of planetary knowledge open to discovery.
Read the reported possibility of travel to planets.
Retain the heavenly railway image in its reported setting.
Hear the delight associated with flight.
shortened: Today I wanted to come here and at the door I saw an airplane rising. It was a very beautiful sight. Truly it is a strange invention. It demonstrates human power, that God has given such power to man that he can fly to heights beyond the capacity of birds.

order.why: Read the reported forecast of universal safe flying as a forecast.
shortened: The science of aviation will make great progress in the immediate future and people will travel at ease from one city to another city without any danger. It will become as popular as automobiles.
Just as now every well to do person has an automobile, then they will have an aeroplane.

order.why: Consider communication and travel as transformed capacities.
Continue the account of transport and communication.
Connect those capacities with the possibility of unity.
shortened: Communication is so easy that in a single moment the East can communicate with the West. A hundred days can be passed in a single day. Ships, in other Manifestations, could only sail near the shore, and if sometimes they did go far they would be missed and could not be traced. Now they cross the ocean.

In the days of the Prophets, Christ and Mohammed, there were many plains and deserts on which no one had traveled, now the trains can go directly and pass over them easily, and the land and sea are so connected with each other that the globe can be traversed in one month.

order.why: Ask who benefits from machines and released time.
shortened: The labor saving machines were given to create leisure for all mankind...

You cannot understand now, how the labor saving machines can produce leisure for mankind because at present they are all in the hands of the financiers and are used only to increase profits, but that will not continue. The workers will come into their due benefit from the machine that is the divine intention, and one cannot continue to violate the law of God.

order.why: Bring theories toward practical action.
shortened: The Tablets of Baha'u'llah are many. The precepts and teachings they contain are universal, covering every subject. He has revealed scientific explanations ranging throughout all the realms of human inquiry and investigation -- astronomy, biology, medical science, etc.

His teachings are universal and the standard for human action. They are not merely theoretical and intended to remain in books. They are the principles of action. Results follow action. Mere theory is fruitless. Of what use is a book upon medicine if it is never taken from the library shelf? When practical activity has been manifested, the teachings of God have borne fruit.

order.why: Recall an aspiration once dismissed as impossible.
Connect ethical and international development.
Read the proposed gathering concerned with religious traditions and unity.
shortened: If this esteemed congress will, as it should and must, promote these beneficent purposes and eliminate these traditions in the possession of religions which are contrary to the divine foundation, the world will become another world, the earthly realm shall become a heavenly realm, the human world shall become the dawning-place of reality, and the rays of the Sun of the celestial realm shall shine upon it. East and West shall be illumined, South and North shall embrace one another, all religions shall seek and speak the truth, and everlasting foundations shall be laid in the world of humanity, and the edifice of the unity of the human race shall rise day by day.

order.why: Consider the anticipated emergence of a renewed humanity.
Follow the reported expectation of new relationships after war.
Read the Palace as the report’s image of teachings, love, and peace.
Join knowledge to service that illumines the world.
Consider the educator’s influence on intellectual development.
shortened: He must likewise lay the foundations of human education, that is, he must so educate human minds and thoughts that they may become capable of substantive progress; that science and knowledge may expand; that the realities of things, the mysteries of the universe and the properties of all that exists may be revealed; that learning, discoveries and major undertakings may day by day increase; and that matters of the intellect may be deduced from and conveyed through the sensible.

order.why: Read revelation through the image of spring.
shortened: In like manner, when the holy Manifestation of God, Who is the Sun of the world of creation, casts His splendour upon the world of hearts, minds, and spirits, a spiritual springtime is ushered in and a new life is unveiled. The power of the matchless springtide appears and its marvellous gifts are beheld. Thus you observe that, with the advent of each of the Manifestations of God, astonishing progress was attained in the realm of human minds, thoughts, and spirits. Consider, for example, the progress that has been achieved in this divine age in the world of minds and thoughts---and this is only the beginning of the dawn!

order.why: Hear the reported account of prophets and the roots of knowledge.
shortened: The Prophets of God have founded the laws of divine civilization. They have been the root and fundamental source of all knowledge.

order.why: Retain the historical argument about Muhammad and learning.
Read the relation drawn between religious reality and knowledge.
shortened: "People have a superstitious respect for certain doctrines which are against science and the wise men of the country have thought that religion is opposed to science. Know thou that the great ethical foundation of knowledge is divine revelation and the basis of religion is reality itself.

order.why: Consider the image of knowledge covering the earth.
shortened: Now, in this glorious age, which is the century of Baha'u'llah, consider how far knowledge and learning have progressed, how fully the mysteries of creation have been unveiled, and how many great undertakings have been embarked upon and are multiplying day by day! Soon will material knowledge and learning, as well as spiritual knowledge, make such progress and display such wonders as to dazzle every eye and to disclose the full meaning of the verse of Isaiah: "for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord."

order.why: Read the unfolding scroll of learning.
Retain the symbolic account of letters of knowledge.
Read the related saying attributed to Imam Sadiq.
shortened: The intention of His Holiness the Truthful One (Imam Sadiq), peace be upon him, is that the sciences and arts that appeared among people up until the previous dispensation were equivalent to two letters, but in the blessed dispensation of the Blessed Beauty, sciences and arts equivalent to the remaining letters - that is, many times over - will appear and emerge.

order.why: Keep the reported numerical formulation in its own version.
Distinguish symbolic spiritual development from literal chronology.
shortened: Aside from the true meaning of this passage which pertains to the power and might of the Cause of God, to the revelation of verses and signs, to the solution of divine problems, to the disclosure of the mysteries of the Holy Book and to the spread of knowledge - each of which is a hundred times greater in this mighty revelation than in any previous one - materially, too, all the learned men of this age agree that the advancements in knowledge, the arts, industries and inventions of this century are equal to those of the last fifty centuries, indeed, even greater than that.

order.why: Retain the reported claim concerning scripture and sciences.
Read mastery of nature as the report’s figurative language.
shortened: Science is the governor of nature and its mysteries, the one agency by which man explores the institutions of material creation. All created things are captives of nature and subject to its laws.

But man through the exercise of his scientific, intellectual power can rise out of this condition, can modify, change and control nature according to his own wishes and uses. Science, so to speak, is the breaker of the laws of nature.

order.why: Return to the expansion of knowledge.
Hear the expectation of further discoveries.
Connects expanding sciences, inventions and discoveries with continuing development.
Read the unveiling of mysteries.
Keep renewal in sciences and weapons within the same horizon.
Consider the scale of change expressed through an age.
shortened: See how, in this day, the scope of sciences and arts hath widened out, and what wondrous technical advances have been made, and to what a high degree the mind's powers have increased, and what stupendous inventions have appeared.

This age is indeed as a hundred other ages: should ye gather the yield of a hundred ages, and set that against the accumulated product of our times, the yield of this one era will prove greater than that of a hundred gone before.

order.why: Compare the reported estimate of a century’s advances.
Read the diamond image for the age.
Hear the expectation of further civilization.
shortened: From the standpoints of both material and spiritual civilization extraordinary progress and development will be witnessed.

In this present cycle there will be an evolution in civilization unparalleled in the history of the world. The world of humanity has, heretofore, been in the stage of infancy; now it is approaching maturity.

order.why: Retain the reported prospect concerning America.
Keep the reported images of transformed materials in context.
shortened: Do you see this Garden? Do you see all these stones? All will be destroyed. But the time will come when these will be renewed, and then they will be fixed for all time. But the people will not be satisfied, but will bring marble.  Even this will not satisfy them. They will bring one brick of silver and one brick of gold.

order.why: Read the expectation of future healing without turning it into present medical advice.
Compare the related expectation concerning food and healing.
Retain the reported prediction about diet.
Turn toward the education of future children.
Continue the hope for their capacities.
Read the reported comparison of future children and present sages.
shortened: O My Letters! Verily I say, immensely exalted is this Day above the days of the Apostles of old. Nay, immeasurable is the difference! You are the witnesses of the Dawn of the promised Day of God. You are the partakers of the mystic chalice of His Revelation.

The secret of the Day that is to come is now concealed. It can neither be divulged nor estimated. The newly born babe of that Day excels the wisest and most venerable men of this time, and the lowliest and most unlearned of that period shall surpass in understanding the most erudite and accomplished divines of this age.

order.why: Connect revelation with fresh scientific insight in the supplied passage.
Make patient scientific work and application explicit.
Read the supplied clarification about evolution and changing knowledge.
shortened: We don't believe man has always had the form of man, but rather that from the outset he was going to evolve into the human form and species and not be a haphazard branch of the ape family. You see our whole approach to each matter is based on the belief that God sends us divinely inspired Educators. What they tell us is fundamentally true; what science tells us today is true, tomorrow may be entirely changed to better explain a new set of facts.

order.why: Keep the horizon of human progress open.
Extend future development to art.
Close with art and the Temple as an early beginning.

questions: How can later generations surpass earlier knowledge while honoring the people who made their learning possible?
What differences matter when reading a symbolic image, a reported forecast, an empirical claim, or guidance about investigation?
What might help moral capacity develop alongside the power of scientific and technical discovery?
How does Bacon’s imagined choice about publishing discoveries illuminate questions of benefit, responsibility, and control?
What would it take for labor-saving inventions to enlarge people’s opportunities for education, service, and a fuller life?
How do the connected subjects of human maturity and science and religion change the questions you would ask about a promising new technology?

references.label: 1 · Francis Bacon · New Atlantis, the account of Salomon’s House
references.note: In Bacon’s fictional research institution, investigators organize experiments, develop discoveries, and deliberate over which findings to publish or keep secret. Its members also pray that their work be put to good uses. Compare this imagined joining of inquiry, power, and responsibility with the compilation’s hopes for discovery and concerns about destructive applications. The text opens questions about who judges benefit and controls knowledge; its arrangements need not be accepted as an ideal.
